 Next ANCHOR Payments Hit NJ Taxpayers: Did You Get Yours?
 More payments are hitting mailboxes and accounts days before a critical ANCHOR application deadline. 
 Jack Slocum , Patch Staff 
 Posted Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 2:15 pm ET The latest round of ANCHOR tax rebates should be hitting New Jersey taxpayers' accounts and mailboxes, as the final deadline to apply for property tax relief approaches. 
 On Oct. 15, the state began ANCHOR property tax relief payments to homeowners and renters under 65. This came roughly two weeks after property taxpayers 65 and over began seeing their rebates on Oct. 1. 
 Applications are still being accepted until Nov. 2. With payments usually not being sent out until 90 days after applications are filed, some residents may not see their slice of the pie until 2027.

 Other residents can expect to receive less money in their ANCHOR payments this year. Since the new budget was passed in July, senior homeowners will no longer receive the $250 bonus they may have gotten in the past.
 Find out what's happening in Across New Jersey for free with the latest updates from Patch. 
 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . With roughly $2 billion set aside for ANCHOR payments, New Jerseyans can still expect to see around $1 billion in 2025 relief payments.
 Those who filed their ANCHOR application by paper can expect to receive their funds by paper check in the mail. Online filers had the option to receive a check or to use direct deposit.
 While Sept. 15 marked the first day ANCHOR payments were sent out, it is also the deadline for applicants to update their banking and address information. Click here to make sure your information is up to date.
 Related: NJ Tax Relief, ANCHOR, Deadlines: What To Know 
 Can I Still Apply? 
 The ANCHOR program, or the Affordable New Jersey Communities for Homeowners and Renters program, offers tax relief for owners and renters in New Jersey, and this year’s relief is based on residents’ 2025 income, age, and residency.
 Most eligible residents will have their application re-filed automatically for them. Those new to the program and people 65+ years old who collect Social Security disability benefits need to file an ANCHOR application on their own.
 The PAS-1 combined application has been available to fill out for eligible people 65 years and older. The application allows people to claim benefits from ANCHOR, Senior Freeze, and the Stay NJ Program (see more on those last two later), all at once, even if they aren't eligible for all of the programs.
 Applicants should prepare their 2025 property tax details, including their County/Municipality Code, Block/Lot/Qualifier, and tax amounts, as well as the gross income reported on their 2024 NJ-1040 when applying.
 To file your ANCHOR application yourself, click here. The deadline to file is Nov. 2.
 See ANCHOR eligibility requirements below:
 Homeowners are eligible if: 
 You were a New Jersey resident in 2025
 You owned and occupied a home in New Jersey that was your principal residence (main home) on Oct. 1, 2025; and
 Your home was subject to property taxes, and
 Your 2025 New Jersey gross income was not more than $250,000.
 Renters are eligible if: 
 You were a New Jersey resident in 2025
 You rented and occupied a residence in New Jersey that was your principal residence (main home) on Oct. 1, 2025
 Your name was on the lease or rental agreement
 You paid rent
 The rental property was subject to local property taxes
 Your 2025 New Jersey gross income was not more than $150,000.
 Those who have their ANCHOR application re-filed automatically by the state should have already received their ANCHOR confirmation letter in the mail .
 The rebate amounts will be the same as last year’s: $450 for renters to $1,500 for homeowners. Senior homeowners can receive up to $1,750, and senior renters can receive up to $700, depending on income.
 Residents can check their ANCHOR benefit status online here .
